targets.title: Design and Evaluation of IPFS: A Storage Layer for the Decentralized Web
targets.authors: Dennis Trautwein, Aravindh Raman, Gareth Tyson, Ignacio Castro, Will Scott, Moritz Schubotz, Bela Gipp, Yiannis Psaras
targets.why_needed: The primary architecture paper for IPFS (libp2p transport, Kademlia location, Bitswap exchange, IPLD linking) with the authors' own measurement of the deployed public network; every later IPFS measurement paper in this domain compares against or extends this baseline.

targets.title: The Eternal Tussle: Exploring the Role of Centralization in IPFS
targets.authors: Yiluo Wei, Dennis Trautwein, Yiannis Psaras, Ignacio Castro, Will Scott, Aravindh Raman, Gareth Tyson
targets.why_needed: Named directly in the domain brief as the target IPFS centralization measurement; states the magnitude by which one indexing service's stored location-record count exceeds the whole DHT's, the load-bearing figure for the claim that content addressing alone does not prevent single-intermediary capture.

targets.title: IPFS in the Fast Lane: Accelerating Record Storage with Optimistic Provide
targets.authors: Dennis Trautwein, Yiluo Wei, Yiannis Psaras, Moritz Schubotz, Ignacio Castro, Bela Gipp, Gareth Tyson
targets.why_needed: States IPFS's own measured publication-latency distribution (median, 90th and 95th percentile) for writing a location record into the Kademlia DHT, and attributes most of that latency to the iterative forwarding sequence; needed as the primary source for any claim about IPFS content-publication latency, since the prior pass carried this figure from a secondary description only.

targets.title: Studying the Workload of a Fully Decentralized Web3 System: IPFS
targets.authors: Pedro Ákos Costa, João Leitão, Yiannis Psaras
targets.why_needed: Independent workload characterization of IPFS content-identifier retrieval and location-record lookup at multi-million-CID scale; the prior pass cited an average and a maximum retrieval-latency figure from this paper's arXiv preprint without opening it, so the full text must be checked against that carried-forward number before it is used again.

targets.title: Challenges in the Decentralised Web: The Mastodon Case
targets.authors: Aravindh Raman, Sagar Joglekar, Emiliano De Cristofaro, Nishanth Sastry, Gareth Tyson
targets.why_needed: Founding measurement of Mastodon/ActivityPub federation concentration, including the simulated-outage figures (largest-connected-component collapse from removing autonomous systems, post share removed by instance outages) that quantify re-concentration with numbers rather than narrative, directly answering the domain's causal-evidence request.

targets.title: Understanding the growth of the Fediverse through the lens of Mastodon
targets.authors: Lucio La Cava, Sergio Greco, Andrea Tagarelli
targets.why_needed: Post-2019 growth and instance-concentration measurement of the fediverse, needed to determine whether Raman et al.'s 2019 concentration figures held, worsened, or improved as the network grew, which the domain brief singles out as the highest-value kind of finding.

targets.title: An evidence-based and critical analysis of the Fediverse decentralization promises
targets.authors: Henrique S. Xavier
targets.why_needed: A named critique testing the fediverse's decentralization claims against measured data; not confirmed in a peer-reviewed venue on DBLP, so its figures need a full-text pass to separate its measurements from its argument before either enters the evidence file.

targets.title: A Herd of Young Mastodonts: the User-Centered Footprints of Newcomers After Twitter Acquisition
targets.authors: Francesco Di Cursi, Chiara Boldrini, Andrea Passarella, Marco Conti
targets.venue: IEEE International Conference on Big Data
targets.why_needed: Measures where a large wave of new users actually settled inside the fediverse's instance topology after a centralized-platform exit event, the direct empirical case of whether an open migration path redistributes users or reconcentrates them onto a few instances.

targets.title: Bluesky and the AT Protocol: Usable Decentralized Social Media
targets.authors: Martin Kleppmann, Paul Frazee, Jake Gold, Jay Graber, Daniel Holmgren, Devin Ivy, Jeromy Johnson, Bryan Newbold, Jaz Volpert
targets.why_needed: The architecture paper for the AT Protocol (account portability, separated hosting/relay/AppView roles, decentralized identifiers), written by the protocol's own designers; every Bluesky concentration measurement compares actual deployment against this design's stated separation of components.

targets.title: Looking AT the Blue Skies of Bluesky
targets.authors: Leonhard Balduf, Saidu Sokoto, Onur Ascigil, Gareth Tyson, Björn Scheuermann, Maciej Korczynski, Ignacio Castro, Michal Król
targets.why_needed: The first large-scale measurement of Bluesky's decomposed architecture, collecting data across every AT Protocol subcomponent (personal data servers, relays, AppViews, labelers) and assessing provider diversity for each; this is the direct 2024 test of whether decomposing a platform into swappable subcomponents actually produces provider diversity or re-concentrates each subcomponent separately.

targets.title: The Rise of Bluesky
targets.authors: Ozgur Can Seckin, Filipi Nascimento Silva, Bao Tran Truong, Sangyeon Kim, Fan Huang, Alessandro Flammini, Filippo Menczer
targets.why_needed: Growth-phase measurement of Bluesky's user base and network structure following its public opening, the temporal complement to Balduf et al.'s architectural snapshot; needed to state whether the measured provider concentration changed as the user count grew by orders of magnitude.

targets.title: An Empirical Analysis of the Nostr Social Network: Decentralization, Availability, and Replication Overhead
targets.authors: Yiluo Wei, Gareth Tyson
targets.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Networking
targets.why_needed: Direct measurement of relay-level concentration in Nostr and the bandwidth/storage overhead of replicating every followed identity's log to every relay a user connects to; the load-bearing source for any Nostr relay-diversity or replication-cost claim in this domain.

targets.title: Understanding User-Generated Content and Communities in Decentralized Web3 Networks: An Empirical Study on Nostr
targets.authors: Shutong Qu, Chunyang Li, Hongzhou Chen, Wei Cai
targets.venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications (TOMCCAP)
targets.why_needed: A second, independent 2026 empirical measurement of Nostr content and community structure, needed to check Wei and Tyson's relay-concentration and availability figures against a differently constructed dataset before either is treated as settled.

targets.title: A Global View of KAD
targets.authors: Moritz Steiner, Taoufik En-Najjary, Ernst W. Biersack
targets.why_needed: Foundational crawl-based measurement of the deployed Kad DHT (eDonkey/eMule's Kademlia implementation, architecturally the same family as the BitTorrent mainline DHT), giving the population, churn, and geographic distribution baseline every later DHT-pollution and Sybil measurement in this domain compares against.

targets.title: Exploiting KAD: Possible Uses and Misuses
targets.authors: Moritz Steiner, Taoufik En-Najjary, Ernst W. Biersack
targets.why_needed: States concrete DHT-poisoning and traffic-redirection attacks demonstrated against a live, deployed Kademlia-family network rather than in simulation; needed to separate theoretical DHT attack surface (already covered by the Sit/Morris and Urdaneta/Pierre/van Steen surveys the prior pass carried) from what was actually shown to work against real deployed nodes.

targets.title: Crawling BitTorrent DHTs for Fun and Profit
targets.authors: Scott Wolchok, J. Alex Halderman
targets.why_needed: Demonstrates that the BitTorrent mainline DHT (distinct from Kad) can be crawled to reconstruct which peers are downloading which content at scale, an operational-privacy failure of a widely deployed unmodified DHT that any content-location design in this architecture must either avoid or account for.

targets.title: Real-World Sybil Attacks in BitTorrent Mainline DHT
targets.authors: Liang Wang, Jussi Kangasharju
targets.why_needed: Measures identity-forgery attacks actually observed in the live BitTorrent mainline DHT rather than injected experimentally, giving a real-deployment base rate for Sybil presence in a DHT with no admission control, the empirical counterpart the domain brief asks for alongside narrative claims.

targets.title: Gossiping with Append-Only Logs in Secure-Scuttlebutt
targets.authors: Anne-Marie Kermarrec, Erick Lavoie, Christian F. Tschudin
targets.why_needed: Measures the per-connection request overhead and message-propagation cost of Secure Scuttlebutt's gossip replication protocol, the specific figures needed to state what a full sync of a new identity actually costs, which the prior pass described only in narrative terms (large initial-sync volume, no measured figure).

targets.title: A Glimpse of the Matrix: Scalability Issues of a New Message-Oriented Data Synchronization Middleware
targets.authors: Florian Jacob, Jan Grashöfer, Hannes Hartenstein
targets.venue: ACM Middleware Demos/Posters (extended version on arXiv)
targets.why_needed: First independent measurement of the deployed public Matrix federation's scaling behavior, needed for the per-room server-resource-consumption figures the domain brief asks for; the prior pass described Matrix's cost only as 'computationally complex' with no cited number.

targets.title: Matrix Decomposition: Analysis of an Access Control Approach on Transaction-based DAGs without Finality
targets.authors: Florian Jacob, Luca Becker, Jan Grashöfer, Hannes Hartenstein
targets.why_needed: Independent formal analysis of Matrix's State Resolution v2 access-control algorithm (the mechanism that makes per-room state resolution computationally expensive), stating what guarantees it does and does not provide; needed to trace the specific mechanism behind the resource-consumption figures in Jacob et al.'s 2019 measurement.

targets.title: Matrix Protocol: A Comprehensive Systematic Mapping Study
targets.authors: José A. P. Martins, Paulo A. L. Rego, José A. F. de Macêdo, Francisco Airton Silva, Vinícius Lagrota
targets.why_needed: 2026 systematic mapping of published Matrix-protocol research, satisfying the domain's requirement for a current survey and providing a bibliography of every scaling and resource-consumption study to check this target list against for completeness.

targets.title: Measuring Freenet in the Wild: Censorship-Resilience under Observation
targets.authors: Stefanie Roos, Benjamin Schiller, Stefan Hacker, Thorsten Strufe
targets.why_needed: Active-monitoring measurement of the deployed Freenet (now Hyphanet) network's concurrent node count and per-node session-length/inter-session-length churn distribution, and of how far an observer can track individual node online-time from outside; the operational-measurement counterpart to the Pitch Black attack paper already read in full, needed to separate Freenet's ordinary churn-driven degradation from its adversarial degradation.

targets.title: Trawling for Tor Hidden Services: Detection, Measurement, Deanonymization
targets.authors: Alex Biryukov, Ivan Pustogarov, Ralf-Philipp Weinmann
targets.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
targets.why_needed: Measures how much of the Tor hidden-service address space could be enumerated and deanonymized using a cheap Sybil attack against the hidden-service directory, the concrete cost/exposure figures needed to evaluate any Tor-based rendezvous mechanism this architecture might reuse for reachability behind NAT.

targets.title: Users Get Routed: Traffic Correlation on Tor by Realistic Adversaries
targets.authors: Aaron Johnson, Chris Wacek, Rob Jansen, Micah Sherr, Paul F. Syverson
targets.why_needed: States measured circuit-compromise probabilities for realistic autonomous-system-level and relay-operator-level adversaries against deployed Tor, as a function of user behavior and time online; the concrete cost figures behind the onion-routing tier's stated adversary model, which the prior pass summarized only as 'over 500ms delay' with no compromise-probability figure.

targets.title: RAPTOR: Routing Attacks on Privacy in Tor
targets.authors: Yixin Sun, Anne Edmundson, Laurent Vanbever, Oscar Li, Jennifer Rexford, Mung Chiang, Prateek Mittal
targets.why_needed: Shows that a network-level (BGP/AS-path) adversary can deanonymize Tor users by manipulating routing itself rather than by running Tor relays, measured against the live Tor network topology; needed because it bounds Tor's anonymity guarantee by an adversary class outside the relay-operator threat model the other Tor measurement papers in this list assume.

targets.title: Changing of the Guards: A Framework for Understanding and Improving Entry Guard Selection in Tor
targets.authors: Tariq Elahi, Kevin S. Bauer, Mashael AlSabah, Roger Dingledine, Ian Goldberg
targets.why_needed: Measures how concentrated the deployed Tor network's entry-guard selection is around a small set of high-bandwidth relays, and the resulting exposure to a guard-operating adversary; the direct guard-concentration figure for any capacity-ordered or bandwidth-weighted relay-selection mechanism this architecture might adopt for its own privacy tiers.

targets.title: Measuring Decentralization in Bitcoin and Ethereum using Multiple Metrics and Granularities
targets.authors: Qinwei Lin, Chao Li, Xifeng Zhao, Xianhai Chen
targets.why_needed: Foundational multi-metric measurement of mining/validation concentration in both Bitcoin and Ethereum at multiple granularities (address, entity, geography), the baseline every later single-metric Ethereum client-diversity or RPC-concentration measurement narrows down from.

targets.title: Unveiling Ethereum's P2P Network: The Role of Chain and Client Diversity
targets.authors: Jiahao Luo
targets.why_needed: Direct 2025 measurement of client-implementation and peer-to-peer network diversity in deployed Ethereum, the specific node-distribution concentration figure named in the domain brief; not yet in a peer-reviewed venue on DBLP, so the full-text pass must confirm its measurement method before any figure is carried forward.

targets.title: SoK: Measuring Blockchain Decentralization
targets.authors: Christina Ovezik, Dimitris Karakostas, Mary Milad, Daniel W. Woods, Aggelos Kiayias
targets.why_needed: 2025 Systematization of Knowledge over every published blockchain-decentralization metric, the survey the domain brief asks for and the source most likely to state whether an academic measurement of RPC-provider concentration (as opposed to mining/validator concentration) exists at all.

targets.title: SoK: A Stratified Approach to Blockchain Decentralization
targets.authors: Christina Ovezik, Dimitris Karakostas, Aggelos Kiayias
targets.why_needed: Earlier, 2024 SoK by the same lead authors proposing the layered (network/consensus/application) decomposition that the 2025 ACNS SoK above builds on; needed to trace which decentralization metrics are original to which paper before citing either.

targets.title: Neither Snow Nor Rain Nor MITM...: An Empirical Analysis of Email Delivery Security
targets.authors: Zakir Durumeric, David Adrian, Ariana Mirian, James Kasten, Elie Bursztein, Nicolas Lidzborski, Kurt Thomas, Vijay Eranti, Michael D. Bailey, J. Alex Halderman
targets.why_needed: Measures SMTP transport-security deployment across the Alexa top million domains' mail infrastructure and across live Gmail-observed inbound/outbound traffic; the closest available primary measurement of email-provider concentration found in this pass (no dedicated academic market-concentration study for email surfaced under any search phrasing tried) and must be read to determine whether it separately reports provider-level traffic share or only security-protocol adoption.
